**Homes go by the river** (pinned promise on Day 1: "first 10 followers get a house on the river"): a row on the south bank, doors facing south, x = C+18 + 17·i, y = river + 21. The six Day 1 plots (P0–P5) stay free for builds.
The most-liked comment of the day gets built, credited on screen: `WISH BY @handle (N♥)`.

At 1,000 followers the village becomes a city (the Day 1 vision is the promise). Stages on the way (`world/state.py` `STAGES`): camp, village from 10, town from 150 (well, market, farm, stone roads), city at 1,000.

**Who lives where, automatically** (`python world/state.py --place handles…`): homeless villagers are housed first, then empty homes go to the next arrival, then the next free plot of the street plan nearest the camp (new streets open south of the first one, 56 apart, linked at both ends); when the plan is full the oldest house nearest the camp gains a storey (level 2 holds 2 households, level 3 holds 4).

**Every building has a road to the camp, every bank a crossing, every door a clear front yard.** `python world/check.py --trees` must pass before any render (the structure has no road on purpose: the mystery).
**Voxel rules:** `core/VOXEL_RULES.md` lists the voxel mistakes made so far (18, each with the rule and whether it is fixed) and a checklist every new model and creature must pass.

**Every creature moves** (owner, 2026-10-30): breathing, neck, head, jaw, tail and wings, never a statue (`core/dragon.py` is the pattern: sculpt once, bend per frame). Tails are physical (`dragon.TailSim`): they lag behind the body, swing through, drag on the ground or gold and climb over what is under them.
Time moves forward: every reel continues from the previous reel's last moment. Nothing disappears without a reason shown on screen.
fixed: The world is generated from fixed seeds in `engine.py` (copied into each day's folder unchanged except for additive fields): `WORLD = 800`, camp centre **C = (400, 400)**, river, trees, rocks, grass and clouds come out identical every run. Never edit seeds, `WORLD`, `CX0/CY0` or the river formula.
Directions: +x = east, −y = north. The river runs west–east about 30–50 units north of the camp.
Scale: a villager is ~11 units tall (sprite scale 0.85), pines 18–27, tent 9, houses ~13, castle ~55, the giant structure ~62, the dragon ~66 long with ~90 wingspan.

Look (from Day 2): the **diorama style** (`_shared/style/STYLE.md`, renderers `episodes/d2-something-woke-up/dio.py` + `episodes/d2-something-woke-up/span.py`) on a **spanning world**: night, glowing turquoise water as the key light, three-tone voxels, bloom; wide shots in perspective with horizon, stars, moon and fog; story shots isometric. No cut-out block. Day 1 used the earlier perspective pixel-voxel look.
Land: the village plateau ends at a wavy cliff x ≈ C−150 (see `span.cliff_x`); the lowland west of it is 34 lower, with a lake where the river's waterfall lands. Forest covers the whole world.

Beyond the world (from 2026-10-30, `episodes/d3-it-moved/glr.py`): in perspective wides the land past the 800 edge is dense forest in the world's autumn mix out to the haze line, and three ranges stand on the horizon: low tree-lined hills, forested hills, and blue-grey mountains with snow caps. Never plain or barren land.

Voice: Days 1–3 · Part 2 edge-tts `en-US-AndrewMultilingualNeural`; **from Day 4 the owner's own "Deep narrator" voice** (Voicebox, Chatterbox on the GPU, `voice/narrate_flow.py --engine chatterbox --base 12`); the same ask at the end of every reel.

# Day 3 — "It moved" (director's treatment, draft 2: tuned for the Reels algorithm)

## Why this draft changed (the evidence)
**Our numbers** (Instagram insights, read 2026-10-29):
| reel | views | viewers | views/viewer | non-followers | likes | comments | saves | shares | follows | follows/viewer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | 353 | 249 | 1.42 | 87 % | 19 | 9 | 2 | 0 | 11 | 4.4 % |
| Day 2 | 1,627 | 1,355 | 1.20 | 97 % | 60 | 24 | 20 | **0** | 39 | 2.9 % |

- Almost everyone who sees us is a stranger (97 %), so **frame 1 must explain the channel** to someone who has
  never heard of it. Day 2's frame 1 said "DAY 2 / SOMETHING WOKE UP", which only makes sense to followers.
- People who watch do follow (2.9-4.4 % is strong) and save (20). **Nobody shares (0).** Sends per reach is the
  signal that carries a reel to new people, so this is the gap to close.
- Rewatches fell from 1.42 to 1.20 views per viewer as the reel got longer and busier. (Average watch time and the
  retention graph are only in the phone app; they would tell us exactly where people leave.)

**The reference channel** (@realm.of.many, 7.4 K followers, same concept): normal reels get 5-16 K views. Their one
breakout (200 K, "Day 2, part 2") is **26 s long**, opens with the payoff as a number ("6 followers → 6 cabins")
over the whole village, then shows each new house with its owner's handle, "new since Part 1: @name", and the
comment wish ("wish by @darkgeniuses: palisade — started"). Its caption ends "Find your house: link in bio" (they
run a website at realmofmany.github.io). Its top comments are people asking for **their own** home type
("Can I have a Blacksmith's house :D?" 1,059 ♥, "may i have a wizards tower" 148 ♥).

**What Instagram ranks Reels on** (Mosseri, Jan 2025, still repeated in 2026 guides): watch time / completion,
sends per reach, likes per reach. Sends matter most for reaching non-followers.

## The director's rules for Day 3, from that
1. **Frame 1 = the rule + the payoff number + motion.** A stranger reads "1 FOLLOWER = 1 VILLAGER" and
   "42 FOLLOWED → 42 HOMES" while something big moves. The rule stays as a small strip under the HUD all the way
   through, for anyone who joins mid-reel.
2. **Shorter: 38 s instead of 60.** Completion and rewatches count more than length. Every beat 2-4 s, a visible
   change at least every 2 s.
3. **Built to be rewatched:** the 42 handles roll by too fast to read in one go ("FIND YOUR NAME 👀"), so people
   pause or replay. The last frame cuts cleanly into the first.
4. **Built to be sent:** personal payoffs people want to show a friend (your name on a house, your wish came true),
   one funny character (the hunchback who waves at everyone), and one jaw-drop image (the dragon's face, the
   black hole, the totems lighting up). One soft line near the end: "SEND THIS TO YOUR FUTURE NEIGHBOUR".
5. **Comments with a personal stake:** show that people who asked to *be* something got it (blacksmith, wizard,
   knight, vampire), so the next viewers comment "can I be…?". The spoken ask stays the canon line.
6. **Sound off still works:** every beat reads from the words on screen; the narrator is shorter and lighter.

## Inputs (INPUTS.md) and owner decisions
- 52 followers → **POP 53**, 42 new villagers, @keelinbb unfollowed.
- Top comment @darrellrasor42 "Enchanted Tiki Island" **7♥** → an original tiki lagoon copied from the owner's
  reference with **no** SpongeBob characters and no SpongeBob name on screen.
- Owner (2026-10-29): the structure sinks and rises far from the village with the new design; the HD scary dragon
  goes into the world; the wanderer (@carlossgarciaah) is a hunchback; the caped villager (@gulalireng) is a vampire
  who turns into a bat and only shows at night; names are shown, not read out; the wizard tower (@huntman225) has a
  mini black hole on top; the fishing hut gets a small boat; it is daytime and the river stops glowing; the tiki
  totems stand at the foot of the cliff, far from the village.

## Places (C = camp centre (400, 400))
| what | where | note |

# Day 3 — "Something waved back" (story cut, draft 3)

A re-cut of Day 3 that uses only what is already built and in the world (the structure, the vampire → bat, the
dragon's embers and the HD dragon, the castle, the knight, the street of 39 homes, the wish homes, the fishing hut
and boat, the tiki lagoon and its totems, the hunchback, the hooded figure). No new models. Same 38 s,
1080×1920. It replaces the narration, the words on screen and a few character placements of `SCRIPT.md`
("It moved", as rendered).

## Why re-cut: what the rendered cut does and where it loses people
Read from `out/day3_strip.png` (1 frame/s) against what Instagram ranks on.
1. **Frame 1 is a number, not a question.** "42 FOLLOWED → 42 HOMES" tells a stranger the result before they care.
   97 % of our viewers are strangers (Day 2 insights), and Instagram now counts viewers who skip in the first 3 s.
2. **12–26 s is a catalogue.** A list card, then seven "ASKED TO BE A …" cuts. Each cut is a label, so nothing pulls
   the viewer into the next one. This is the longest stretch of the reel and the one most likely to lose people.
3. **No one to follow.** The story is about "the world", so there is no character to root for or send to a friend.
4. **The ending is not earned.** The hooded figure appears for the first time at 33 s with no link to anything
   before it, so "Someone is watching" has no setup.
5. **Weak send prompt.** "Send this to your future neighbour" names nobody. Day 2 got **0 shares**, and shares
   (sends per reach) are what carry a reel to new people.

## The fix: one hero, one chain, one threat
- **Hero: the hunchback (@carlossgarciaah)**, the stranger who didn't want a house, only to say hi to everyone.
  It's already built and waving, it's funny, and everyone has a friend like that (the send).
- **The catalogue becomes a walk.** The hunchback says hi to each wish home and each one answers in its own way
  (anvil sparks, the black hole pulses, the knight's armour clanks, the oar splashes, the basement hatch creaks
  open). Same credits, but now every cut is a step in a story.
- **The threat pays off the hero's habit.** The hunchback waves at the far tower, and the hooded figure waves back.
  That's the cliffhanger, and the theory bait for Day 4.
- **Every line causes the next** (skill rule): strangers came → the tower sank → one stranger isn't human →
  sunrise: the dragon changed → the tower came back → homes for everyone → one stranger didn't want a home → it
  said hi to everyone → everyone said hi back → even the totems → it waved at the tower → something waved back.

Read alone, without pictures, the narration tells the whole story:
> Forty-two strangers moved in. The tower... didn't like it. One of them... isn't human. At sunrise, the dragon
> shed its skin. And far away... the tower came back. We built forty-two homes. Find yours. One stranger didn't
> want a house... only to say hi to everyone. And everyone said hi back. The top comment wished for a tiki island.
> Even its totems said hi. Then the hunchback waved at the tower. Something... waved back. Comment: what do you
> want the world to have?

85 words in 38 s (about 2.2 words a second), with silence under the dragon, the rise and the walk.

| 3.2–5.6 | not human | iso close on river house 4's roof (as 2.5–5) | the vampire watches the sky turn pink; puff at 4.6, a bat flies to the moon | `@GULALIRENG` / `NOT HUMAN` | 3.3 "One of them... isn't human." | puff, bat wings |
| 5.6–9.8 | dragon | push from the castle to the keep (as 5–9.5) | the blocky dragon bursts into embers (6.6); the HD dragon stands and roars (7.4) | `YESTERDAY: 12` → `TODAY: 53` (counter) | 5.8 "At sunrise, the dragon shed its skin." | embers, roar, ticks, dawn birds |
| 9.8–12.2 | it came back | persp wide to the NE (as 9.5–12) | the structure rises. **NEW Easter egg:** the hooded figure stands on the tower for 8 frames (10.9–11.2) | `IT CAME BACK.` | 10.0 "And far away... the tower came back." | distant rumble, water rush |
| 12.2–15.1 | homes | iso, follows the street west → east (as 12–18, faster) | homes rise one by one; the NEW FOLLOWERS card scrolls all 42 handles **in 2.8 s** (too fast to read: pause or rewatch) | `42 NEW HOMES` · `FIND YOUR NAME 👀` | 12.4 "We built forty-two homes. Find yours." | ping, a rising note per home, hammering |

| 35.2–38 | ask + loop | crane out to the wide on the structure (as 35.2–38) | — | `COMMENT: WHAT DO YOU WANT THE WORLD TO HAVE?` · bottom bar `SEND THIS TO THE FRIEND WHO SAYS HI TO EVERYONE 👋` | 35.4 "Comment: what do you want the world to have?" | closing chime after the line |

**Loop:** it ends on the structure at a wide and opens on the structure close, so a replay feels continuous, and
"Forty-two strangers moved in" works straight after the ask.

## Why each piece is there (the algorithm, and channels like ours)
| signal | what Instagram measures | how this cut earns it |
|---|---|---|
| **skip rate / hook** | viewers who leave in the first 3 s | the voice starts at 0.2 s (the Emplifi study found speech in the first 3 s lifted 10-second retention by ~25 % over music); frame 0 has the rule and a stranger-ready line ("42 strangers moved in") while the structure moves |
| **watch time** | how long people stay, how many finish | every beat opens a question the next one answers (why did the tower sink? who isn't human? what will the hunchback do?), and the biggest one ("waved back") is held to the last 5 s |
| **rewatches** | views per viewer (fell from 1.42 on Day 1 to 1.20 on Day 2) | the 42 names scroll too fast to read; the hooded figure hides in the 10.9 s wide for 8 frames (pinned comment: "did you spot it before the end?"); a seamless loop |
| **sends per reach** | DMs and shares (Day 2: 0) | a hero people already know from their own lives ("the friend who says hi to everyone") and a send line that names that friend; your-name-on-a-house payoffs |
| **comments** | comments per reach | theory bait ("who's on the tower?") plus the people who asked to *be* someone getting it, so the next viewers ask "can I be…?". This is what @realm.of.many's 1,059-like top comment was: a viewer asking for their own blacksmith house |
| **follows** | follows per viewer (2.9–4.4 % for us, strong) | the rule stays on screen all reel; the cliffhanger gives a reason to follow for Day 4 |

From @realm.of.many (same concept, 7.4K followers): their breakout reel was 26 s and paid people off by name. We
keep 38 s because this cut is one story with a payoff at the end. If the trial version below drops off early, cut
the dragon beat to 3 s and the lagoon to 5 s (≈ 33 s).

## Hook A/B (post one as a trial reel, shown only to non-followers)
- **A (main):** as above. Frame 0: `42 STRANGERS MOVED IN`, voice "Forty-two strangers moved in."
- **B (flash-forward):** open on the 33.5 s shot (the hooded figure raising its hand) for 1.2 s with
  `SOMETHING IN MY VILLAGE WAVED BACK`, voice "Something in my village waved back... here's how." Then hard cut to 0.0
  of A. Costs one extra line and 1.2 s.
Post B as the trial; if its 3-second hold beats A by a clear margin within 24 h, share it to followers. Otherwise
post A.

## Cover, caption, pinned comment
- **Cover:** the HD dragon's face (as now), or the tower top with the hooded figure's raised hand; big `DAY 3`, under
  it `SOMETHING WAVED BACK`. Keep both lines inside the 3:4 grid crop.
- **Caption (first line is the hook):**
  > Day 3. 42 strangers moved in. One of them says hi to everyone… and something waved back. 👀 Find your name.
  >
  > Before dawn the tower sank, and came back far away. One stranger isn't human 🧛 At sunrise the dragon shed its skin 🐉
  >
  > 👋 The hunchback who says hi to everyone: @carlossgarciaah
  > ⚒️ You asked to be someone, so you are: blacksmith @michi_gellrich, chef @abdu.llah02058, wizard (with a tiny black hole) @huntman225, knight @just_t4te, fishermen @hudsonryder_ & @maloyowen, hidden basement @themetalkiddo2, creature of the night @gulalireng
  > 🗿 Top comment (7♥): a tiki island, wished by @darrellrasor42
  > 🕵️ Best theory, by @q_saliaz: "whoever commanded the dragon"… so who's on the tower?
  >
  > Follow → you move in, with your name on a house.
  > Most-liked comment gets built next.
  > 1,000 followers → a city.
  >
  > 💬 Comment: what do you want the world to have?
  >
  > #pixelart #voxelart #worldbuilding #cozygames #simulation #indiegame #citybuilder #pixelartist #gamedev #realmpixels

- **Pinned comment:** "Who's on the tower? 👀 Best theory gets built into Day 4. (Did you spot it before the end?)"
- **Second comment:** "Comment what YOU want to be in the village 👇 (blacksmith? wizard? vampire?)"

# Day 3 · Part 2 — "The gold rumour" (director's treatment, draft 1)

42.5 s, 1080×1920, 30 fps. **The same day as Day 3, from afternoon to night** (owner, 2026-10-30): Day 3 ran from
night through sunrise into the day; this part picks up that afternoon and ends at night. Everything from Day 3 is in
place (the structure on the north-east hills, the HD dragon on the keep, the street, the tiki lagoon). HUD
`DAY 3 · PART 2` · `POP 53+N`; the folder is `day4/` because it is the fourth reel. New followers are slots (`N`,
`@NEW1`, `@NEW2`) until `INPUTS.md` is filled.

## The story in one breath
That afternoon, the tower starts spilling gold. The coins wash down the river past the castle, where the dragon notices. The
hunchback finds one first and runs to tell everyone: seen from the villagers' own eyes, new homes burst out of the
ground, the farm's crops shoot up and the dogs chase it off, and by the tent a horse stable rises. By sunset, the rumour has grown from "a gold coin" into "a castle with a waterfall of gold". That night
the villagers meet in secret in the hidden basement. The wizard has a plan. The farm dogs smell the coin and point
to the hills. A search party sets off by lantern light. Near the tower the coins stop. The hooded figure flicks one
last coin down to them: it was bait. And the dragon takes off after the gold too.

- **Dramatic question:** where is the gold coming from, and who gets to it first?
- **Visual thesis (photographable):** one coin in one hand grows into a line of lanterns climbing to the tower.
- **Feeling:** greed and excitement turning to dread; comedy in the middle (the rumour), a threat at the end.
- **Why watch today:** gold, a funny rumour, your name on a house, a secret mission. **Why come back tomorrow:**
  do they go in, and what does the dragon do? Viewers vote.

## Narration, read alone (it has to tell the story without pictures)
> This morning, the tower moved. Now... it's spilling gold. The coins washed down the river... and the dragon
> noticed. But the hunchback found one first... and ran past forty new homes... through the new farm... to tell
> everyone. By sunset, one coin... was a waterfall of gold. That night... they met in secret. The wizard had a plan. The dogs
> smelled the coin... and pointed to the hills. Someone... wanted them to come. And the dragon wants the gold too.
> Comment: what do you want the world to have?

16 lines, 87 words in 42.5 s (about 2 words a second); silent under the stable, the rumour bubbles, the night
falling and the moment the coins stop. "Forty" is spoken as the real `N`. Each line causes the next; every character is set up
before a line refers to them (the dragon and the hunchback are known from Day 3, the dogs are shown at 12 s before the
line at 28 s).

## How this cut earns watch time (research, then the rules it gives)
**What Instagram measures** (Mosseri's January 2025 signals, still repeated in 2026 guides): watch time, likes per
reach and sends per reach, with skip rate (leaving in the first 3 s) replacing view rate. Replays count in the
retention graph: a spike means people scrubbed back to rewatch a moment.

**What holds people in short serial stories** (practitioner guides and our own Day 1-3 numbers; no platform study
exists, so treat these as working rules, not law):
- **Open loops:** a question the viewer wants answered keeps them watching (the curiosity gap; the Zeigarnik effect
  behind it has mixed replications). Overuse confuses, and a loop never paid off reads as clickbait.
- **Each part pays off the last cliffhanger and opens a new one**, with a one-line recap for viewers who missed the
  last part. A viewer who lands on Part 4 goes to the profile for Parts 1-3 (follows).
- **Short and dense beats long and slow:** completion rate matters more than length. A reel that loops seamlessly
  earns replays.
- **Speech in the first 3 s** lifted 10-second retention by ~25 % over music (Emplifi study).

**The rules for this part, from that:**
1. **The loop ladder: at least two questions open at every second, never more than three.** Open the next before
   closing the last.
   | loop | opened | closed |
   |---|---|---|
   | Why is the tower spilling gold? | 1.6 s | 35.7 s (it's bait) |
   | The dragon noticed: what will it do? | 5.4 s | 37.4 s (it takes off) |
   | Who gets the first coin? | 3.4 s | 6.9 s (the hunchback) |
   | What will the village do with the news? | 9.6 s | 26.8 s (a secret plan) |
   | How big does the rumour get? | 14.8 s | 21.0 s (a waterfall of gold) |
   | Where are they going? | 26.8 s | 31.0 s (the dogs point to the hills) |
   | **Should they go in?** | 39.5 s | Part 3, decided by comments |
2. **Recap in five words:** "This morning, the tower moved." Viewers who missed Day 3 are oriented; strangers get the
   rule strip.
3. **Change checkpoints** (skill rule): question at 0-1 s, cut and new picture at 3.0, the find at 6.9, the first
   payoff (homes, farm, stable, seen from the ground) at 9.5-14.6, then a visible change at least every 2 s.
4. **Every follower payoff is inside the story,** not a list: new homes rise around a new follower, seen from their
   eyes, as the hunchback runs past; the two
   oldest new followers pass the rumour on, with their handles under their speech bubbles; the wish homes' owners
   become the search party.
5. **Rewatch bait:** the hooded figure is already on the tower for 6 frames at 2.2 s, before the coins have even
   reached the river (pinned comment: "who was on the tower at 0:02?"); the new handles scroll too fast to read;
   the rumour bubbles escalate too fast to read every word; the last frame is the first frame's camera.
6. **Send bait:** the rumour is the "friend who exaggerates everything" gag. End bar:
   `SEND THIS TO THE FRIEND WHO EXAGGERATES EVERYTHING`.
7. **Comment bait with a stake:** a yes/no decision for Part 3 ("Should they go in?") plus "comment I'M IN to join
   the search party". Votes and joining are cheaper to comment than an idea, so more people do it.
8. **Silence before the line that matters** (skill rule 3): the coin clinking that runs under the whole reel stops at
   34.4 s. The silence *is* the story ("the coins stopped"), then "Someone... wanted them to come."
9. **Narration that contradicts the picture** (skill rule 4): "they met in secret" lands on the black cat watching
   them.

- **Buildings:** red barn with white trim and a hay loft door (open), farmhouse with a porch and chimney smoke,
  windmill (blades turning: motion in every farm shot), scarecrow, hay bales, water trough, chicken coop with a ramp.
- **Livestock** (pairs at least, as @tg.jhonlloyd asked): 2 cows (black-and-white and brown), 4 sheep (wool as
  bobbly fine voxels, black faces), 6 chickens + a rooster, all idling (heads down grazing, ears and tails flicking).
- **Two dogs that protect it:** a black-and-white sheepdog and a golden one. They patrol the fence line at a trot,
  sit by the gate between rounds, and bark (head up, mouth open, tail stiff) at anything that crosses the fence.
- Fence: split-rail around the pasture, a gate on Farm Lane.

## The gold coins: how they glow (owner, 2026-10-30)
Coins are always emissive, never just lit, and brighter the darker it gets:
- **Model:** fine voxels (vs 0.25), a disc ~1.2 units across with a raised rim; three golds per coin: core
  (255, 214, 90), rim (226, 160, 40), stamped face a shade darker (200, 138, 36).
- **Afternoon (0-14.6 s): glow and shimmer.** Emission at about half strength even in full sun (the Day 3 day
  environment turns emission down; coins keep their own floor). Each coin **shimmers** as it spins: its brightness
  follows its tilt to the sun (0.6-1.0, a few times a second, every coin out of phase), plus a white-gold star glint
  (255, 248, 210) for one or two frames when its face catches the sun. No halo by day, so they stay crisp.
- **Sunset (14.6-22.4 s):** emission rises with the falling light; a small halo starts round piles and the coin film.
- **Night (from 22.4 s): glow much more.** Emission ×2.5-3 over the day level (colours divided by the bloom gain, as
  for the falls), a gold halo through the bloom, and **gold light spill** on the water and stone within ~6 units

  in the dark (shot 7b), the coin at the hunchback's feet lights its face from below (8b). The shimmer keeps running,
  slower and softer.
- When the gold stops at 34.4 s, the falls' glow drains out over ~0.5 s: the light dropping is part of the silence.

# Day 4 — "The Gold Below" (director's treatment, draft 3, 2026-10-31)
About 58 s (draft 3: the voice comes first and the shots are cut to it; the shot table's times below are draft 2's
and get re-cut to "The voice" beat times), 1080×1920, 30 fps, rendered with the OpenGL renderer on the GPU (`glr.py`; `glr.INTERIOR = True` for the
shots below ground). The folder is `day5/` because this is the fifth reel (`day4/` is Day 3 · Part 2). HUD `DAY 4` ·
`POP` counting **63 → 74**. It picks up the same night Day 3 · Part 2 ended: the dragon flew to the structure after the
gold, and the search party stood at its foot with their lanterns.

**Draft 2 adds** (owner, 2026-10-31): the new followers arrive by **floating pirate ships** and come down by
**parachute**; they build a **city hall** and a **church with a huge bell**, and someone becomes its **priest**; the
village's new homes are laid out **round the castle like Paris round the Eiffel Tower** (plan: `out/paris_plan.png`,
`paris_plan.py`); Andrew reads with **emotion per beat**, flowing (`voice/narrate_flow.py`, draft 3).

## Draft 4: the hook rewritten as context → lean → snapback (owner, 2026-10-31)
Rewritten with the Triple Hook method (skill: "The hook"; `style-ref/kallawaymarketing/HOOKS.md`). Same three beat
slots, so every later shot and sound stays keyed to its beat; beats file `voice_test/beats_d4_hook.json`, heartbeat
`voice_test/bpm_d4.json` unchanged, take to go in `voice_test/deep_v3/` (day5.py switches to it when it exists).

| | was (rendered, deep_v2) | now |
|---|---|---|
| beat 0 | DREAD "Last night, the dragon followed the gold. Then it went for a swim." | NARR **context** "Sixty-three followers live up here." + **lean** "Under them, our dragon sank into molten gold." |
| beat 1 | DREAD "It went under, and didn't come up." | DREAD (lean, deeper) "It didn't come up." |
| beat 2 | HYPE "Then it came back, bigger!" (at 7.9 s) | HYPE **snapback** "Then it came back up... bigger!" (about 6.5-7 s) |

**Hook test** (the lines alone): *Sixty-three followers live up here. Under them, our dragon sank into molten gold. It
didn't come up. Then it came back up... bigger!*
- Context clear to a stranger? Yes: a world where followers live, a dragon under them, gold. Before: "Last night"
  told a stranger nothing, and nothing in the voice said what this world is.
- Lean? Yes: "sank into molten gold", "didn't come up": the viewer leans towards *it's dead*.
- Snapback? Yes: it comes back *bigger*. The old hook had the same twist, but it came after the context it
  never gave.
- Bonus: "up here" sets up the party before "Up top, we felt it" (beat 4) refers to them, and the number is proof
  that ticks: POP 63 in the HUD, 74 after the parachutes. The ending ("It's awake. Run, or fight?") now loops onto the
  people it threatens.
- Not reached: the snapback lands at ~6.5-7 s, not 3-5 s. The dive needs about 2.4 s on screen, and the owner's rule
  keeps the dip voiced. That is still about 1 s earlier than before, and the context now comes first.

**Picture and text** (in `day5.py`, active with a take whose beat 0 has "Under"):
- New shot **0 up here** (`top`, 0 → the word "Under"): the nine with lanterns at the structure's foot at night,
  Part 2's last place, the new city not yet built, slow push in `(36, 2.6 → 3.4, c5, 60 → 62)`. Headline
  `1 FOLLOWER = 1 VILLAGER` in gold at y 430, scale 6, saying what the voice says. A subject in the first frame (people
  with lanterns), not scenery.
- Hard cut on "Under them" to the hall: shot 1 starts there; the dive (`FX.dive`), splash, gloop and growl start
  from that word instead of fixed times. Wide → ECU, two size steps; lantern light → molten light.
- Everything else is unchanged.

To do: voice beats 0-2 with the Deep narrator into `deep_v3` (copy deep_v2's beats 3-17, or re-voice all 18 for an
even read), run `voice/heartbeat.py`, run Whisper ("Sixty-three" and "sank" must be heard right), then make stills of
shots 0-3 and get the owner's OK before any render.

## The story in one breath
Last night the dragon followed the gold down into the hoard. It walks into the pool of molten gold and goes under.
Two seconds of nothing. Then it bursts out bigger, and the gold doesn't drip off: it soaks in, and the dragon turns
crimson. Up top the search party feels the bang; the floor opens and nine of them go down a spiral stair.
**Meanwhile, the gold rumour has reached the sky.** Pirate airships come out of the clouds and drop eleven new
villagers by parachute onto the castle lawn (one lands in the river). Below, the party passes a blinking eye, tiny
staring fae and a chest that bites. Above, the newcomers don't sleep: by dawn there is a city hall, a church, and a
bell big enough for the whole valley. Below, the party finds the dragon asleep on the gold, exactly as @j_adame21
wished on Day 1. They tiptoe. The cat pulls a coin; nothing falls; everyone breathes out. **Then, up top, the new
priest rings the first bell.** The coins shiver, the mound comes down, a coin rolls to the dragon's nose, and it
opens one eye.
- **Dramatic question:** what did the gold make of the dragon, and can they take some without waking it?
- **Visual thesis (photographable):** the bell swings up top, and down below a mountain of gold shivers.
- **The engine of the reel is dramatic irony:** the viewer knows the dragon is down there and the village up top
  doesn't. Every cut back to the celebration makes the danger below bigger. The bell joins the two threads: the
  village's happiest moment causes the disaster.
- **Feeling:** dread → awe → joy (the arrivals) → creepy wonder → comedy (the cat, the fake relief) → shock.
- **Why watch today:** a transformation, sky pirates, your name on a parachute, a new city, a cat. **Why come back:**
  run or fight? And the pirates came for the gold too.

## Narration, read alone (draft 3, Andrew; it has to tell the story without pictures)
> Last night, the dragon followed the gold. Then it went for a swim. *(silence)* It came back... bigger! The gold
> didn't drip off. It soaked in. Up top, we felt it. The floor just opened. Nine of us went down. I went last. Someone
> had to hold the lantern. Meanwhile, the gold rumour reached the sky. Pirate ships! And they brought eleven new
> villagers. Their landing plan? Jump. One missed. Below us, something big blinked. Tiny people, staring. And the
> chest bit back! Up top, the new ones didn't sleep. A city hall. A church. And a giant bell. Then, the last door. And
> there it lay. Asleep, on all of it. The plan? One coin each. Don't. Wake. It. Everyone was careful. Except the cat.
> *(the trickle stops)* Phew. Up top, the first bell. *(BONG)* Avalanche! *(silence)* Nobody move. It's awake. Run, or
> fight? Comment. You decide.

17 beats, 142 words in ~56 s (2.56 words a second, as even as the viral reference: see "The voice"). Each line causes
the next; the pirates are set up by the rumour (Day 3 · Part 2), the cat by Part 2 and two shots on the way down, the
priest by the church. Short planned pauses (≤ 1.2 s): the trickle stopping, the BONG, after the avalanche; the
dip is no longer silent (owner): a dread line runs over the still pool.

## Rules this cut follows
- **Intercutting:** below, above, below, above. Every cut to the surface ends on something that matters below (the
  bell is hoisted, then rung). A cut in either direction happens at least every 8 s, so neither thread goes cold.
- **Loop ladder** (two or three questions open at every second):
  | loop | opened | closed |
  |---|---|---|

## The voice (draft 3): story beats in one breath, voice first
**Owner's pick (2026-10-31): their own Deep narrator voice** (`voice_test/deep_chatterbox_full/take.wav`, 61 s,
2.51 words/s, evenness 0.33, longest pause 0.84 s; subtitles `subs.json`). Andrew's take stays as the fallback.
The owner heard draft 2's line-by-line take as cut up ("it just cuts and continues randomly"). The causes, all in
how the lines were stitched, not in the Andrew model:
1. one voice call per line, so every line started fresh and ended on a full stop: 24 takes, not one read;
2. big mood jumps (+22 Hz to −16 Hz) with a different EQ per mood, like changing microphones line to line;
3. lines pinned to shot times: slow lines overran and got shoved together 0.25 s apart, while other gaps ran 3-5 s;
4. hard silence trimming that cut the breaths, so the voice dropped into dead air.
**The fix** (`voice/narrate_flow.py`): each story beat (2-5 lines) is one call, so Andrew's own intonation carries
across the lines; moods move speed and pitch only a little (±8 %, ±6 Hz) and the contrast comes from each beat's level
(−8 dB dread to +1.5 dB hype; the pauses between beats hide the change); breaths are kept, a quiet room tone and a
short room reflection run under everything; the beats follow each other with an even 0.45 s breath (voice first),
with only the planned holds longer: 0.9 s for the trickle stopping and for the BONG, 1.2 s after the avalanche. The
dip's 2 s silence is now a line (owner, 2026-10-31: "remove the 2 sec silence and fill it with voice"): "It went

## Why parachutes, not gliders
The newcomers have to land on exact plots in a dense quarter. Round parachutes come down slowly and nearly straight,
read clearly from above and from the side, give each handle a big canopy to be stitched on, and let eleven open one
after another in a pattern (the "pop pop pop" moment). Gliders need speed and a long run in: they would cross the
frame too fast for the names to read and would need a runway in the middle of a city. One gag uses that: the last
canopy catches the wind and lands in the river.

# Day 5 — "The Priest's Bell" (director's treatment, draft 5.1, 2026-11-03)

**Draft 5.1 (2026-11-03): the scoring fixes.** Scored with `ig-reel` (`hookscore.py`, `beats.py` at 204 wpm) and
the director checks (section "Scores"). Fixed: the first line carries the stakes ("until the dragon comes"), "Day
five" moved to the title card only, the knight named out loud (Tate), the four beats over 4 s split, a recap in
threes before the ask, the last line echoes the hook so the reel loops, and the `DAY 6 · RING 3/30` end card is
back. The hook's pause moved: "until the dragon comes" is now the lean and "Our bell just woke it." the snapback,
so the turn lands at ~4.5 s.

**Draft 5 (2026-11-03), after the audit of both accounts.** Draft 4 (in git) told the right secret but carried too
much: pirates robbing the hoard, the dragon loose over the city, a caravan, an escaping airship, and about ten new
builds. Day 4 lost strangers for the same reason, and three days without a post now cost more than any shot. Draft 5
keeps the owner's secret (our own priest rang the bell, under a spell, with the hooded one behind him) and tells it
in @myworld.skill's shape, in our own words:
- **One day, one chain, told by me** (@realm.pixels, the lantern-bearer, already in the hoard): present tense, first
  person, inside the action. Morning in the hoard → the fight → follow the thread → dusk in the bell tower.
- **Commenters by name with their likes**, answered by the story: @liprontea's FIGHT (5♥) decides the fight,
  @just_t4te's paladin wish comes true, @stardust_f48's "friends with the dragon" turns out possible.
- **The newcomers welcomed by name** (five in, two out: four dark homes light up again, one new house; owner 2026-11-03).
- **The clock spoken early** (8 s) and paid at the end: ring two, twenty-eight left.
- **Cut from draft 4:** the pirates' robbery, the dragon in open sky, the caravan, the escaping ship. The why of the
  countdown is now simple: **the bell feeds a spell on the dragon**; each ring tightens it, on ring 30 it obeys.
- **Built new:** the priest and the belfry, the fire, the paladin armour (a recolour), the violet smoke and thread.
  Everything else exists.

FIGHT won the vote (`INPUTS.md`), so there is one version. About 66 s (`beats.py`) to 78 s (our estimate with every pause), 1080×1920, 30 fps. Folder
`episodes/d5-the-priests-bell/` (reel 6, script `day6.py`).

It opens on Day 4's last moment: the bell has rung, the coins have come down, the crimson dragon has opened one eye.
The search party (me with the lantern, eight of you, the cat) stands in the hoard. Up top, the city stands in the dawn.

## The story in one breath
Seventy-six of you live in my city until the dragon comes, and our bell just woke it: somebody rang it on purpose. Every ring wakes it more, and on the thirtieth it comes
for the city. Down in the hoard, as you voted, our knight fights: its fire nearly breaks his shield, but a beam of
the morning sun makes him the paladin he wished to be, and where his light falls, violet smoke burns off the dragon.
It was never angry; it is under a spell. A violet thread runs from its horns up through the rock. I follow it up
through the city, past the newcomers' houses, into our own bell tower, where at dusk our own priest, eyes glowing,
pulls the rope, and something tall behind him holds the thread. Ring two. Twenty-eight left.
- **Dramatic question:** who rang the bell on purpose, and can the city stop it before the thirtieth ring?
- **Visual thesis:** a violet thread running from the dragon's horns up through the rock to the bell rope in our
  priest's glowing hands.
- **Feeling:** dread → courage → wonder (the paladin) → a turn (the dragon is a victim) → suspense (the climb) → the
  reveal.
- **Why watch today:** the vote's fight, a wish come true, who rang the bell. **Why come back:** free the priest or
  hunt the thing behind him; twenty-eight rings left.

## The story through the Loop Engine (and Story Skills' scene tools)
**The reel's Big Question:** who rang the bell on purpose? Asked at ~6 s, answered at ~64 s (our own priest), and
deepened at ~67 s (something behind him holds the thread). **Expected:** the pirates, or the hooded one himself.
**Real:** one of us, spellbound. **Planted by:** Day 4 never showing who rang it; the hooded one on Day 3's tower and
in Day 4's Fae arch.

**Stakes line:** seventy-six followers live in a city whose bell, each time it rings, wakes the dragon a little more;
on the thirtieth ring it comes for them (ring 1 rang on Day 4, ring 2 rings at dusk tonight).

**Try/fail chain** (Story Skills `scene-craft`, try-fail): try 1, the knight's shield → **no-and** (it holds, barely,
and the fire keeps coming); try 2, the sun → **yes-but** (the dragon calms, but it was a spell, a worse problem);
try 3, follow the thread → **yes-but** (we find who rings it, and it's ours, and something worse stands behind him).
The crisis (free the priest or hunt the thing behind him) goes to the comments. The reel ends on a **revelation**
hook, then a **question**.

| loop | time (est.) | stakes | question | expected (A) | real (B) | rehook line | text line |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 = hook | 0-8 | 76 followers' city, until the dragon comes | when will it come? who woke it? | some day, far off | now: our bell woke it, on purpose | "Every ring wakes it a little more." | `1 FOLLOWER = 1 VILLAGER` → `UNTIL THE DRAGON COMES` → `OUR BELL JUST WOKE IT.` → `ON PURPOSE.` |
| L1b clock | 7-17 | the city, ring 1/30; every follower a house on the wall | will it hold by ring 30? | — | (the series) | "Right now, I'm in its hoard." | `RING 1/30` → `FOLLOW = 1 MORE HOUSE ON THE WALL` |
| L2 | 17-36 | the knight, the party | will the shield hold? | it breaks | it holds, barely; the sun makes him a paladin | "And where his light falls..." | `YOU VOTED: FIGHT` → `PALADIN OF THE SUN` |
| L3 | 36-46 | the dragon | why is it so angry? | it's a monster | it's spellbound | "A thin violet thread..." | `IT WAS UNDER A SPELL.` |
| L4 | 46-63 | the city, the newcomers | where does the thread go? | the hooded one's lair | our own bell tower, our own priest | "And behind him..." | `OUR OWN PRIEST.` |
| close | 63-71 | the city, the series | who holds the thread? | — | something tall; ring two | "Free the priest... or hunt the thing behind him?" | `RING 2/30` → `28 RINGS LEFT` → the ask |

**Beat sheet**, every joint a BUT or a THEREFORE:
1. Seventy-six of you live here, until the dragon comes (the stakes).
2. BUT our bell just woke it.
3. BUT somebody rang it on purpose.
4. THEREFORE every ring wakes it more; on the thirtieth it comes for the city.
5. THEREFORE every follower is one more house on the wall.
6. BUT right now I'm in its hoard, and you voted fight.
7. THEREFORE our knight steps up.
8. BUT its fire nearly breaks his shield.
9. BUT the sun lands on his sword, and he becomes a paladin of the sun.
10. THEREFORE his light burns violet smoke off the dragon.
11. BUT that means it was never angry: it's under a spell (so maybe Stardust can be its friend).
12. THEREFORE I follow the violet thread up through the rock and the city, past three new houses.
13. BUT it leads into our own bell tower, to our own priest, eyes glowing.
14. BUT something tall behind him holds the thread, and the bell rings: ring two.
15. THEREFORE, a paladin, a spell, a priest (the recap): free the priest, or hunt the thing behind him? Ring two:
    twenty-eight left until the dragon comes (the ask, then the loop back to the first line).

### Story checks (skill `storytelling.md`)
| test | result |
|---|---|
| stakes: who, what's at risk, the clock by 8 s | ✓ who and risk in the first line (3 s), the clock on the HUD from 0 s and spoken at ~11 s |

| gap: never zero open questions | ✓ "who rang it" stays open from 6 s to 64 s |

## The hook: context → lean → snapback (0-8 s)
**Text first:** `1 FOLLOWER = 1 VILLAGER` big in gold (y 430) with the `DAY 5` title card from 0.0 to 1.5 s; then
`UNTIL THE DRAGON COMES` (DRAGON in gold) from 1.5 s, leading the voice; on the snapback `OUR BELL JUST WOKE IT.`;
on the rehook `ON PURPOSE.`

**Hook test** (the lines alone): *Seventy-six of you live here... until the dragon comes. ... Our bell just woke it.
Somebody rang it on purpose.* Context clear to a stranger? Yes (followers live here; a dragon will come). Lean? Yes
